guides.title: Body temperature
guides.message: Elevated temperature (38.06 °C). Possible fever or hyperthermia. Notify the medical team.
guides.action: Possible fever or hyperthermia: alert the physician.
steps: Remove clothing layers / increase local ventilation.
Hydrate.
Look for symptoms of infection.
Notify the physician.
Repeat every 15 min.

guides.title: Systolic pressure
guides.message: Blood pressure outside optimal range (125/75 mmHg). Check hydration and exercise load.
guides.action: Review hydration, exercise (ARED) and fluid shift toward the head.
steps: Repeat at rest after 5 min, arm at heart level.
Check hydration and sodium.
Review exercise load.
Repeat in 1–2 h.

guides.title: Sleep last night
guides.message: Sleep below recommended (6.4 h). Review your rest routine.
steps: Avoid bright light before sleeping (sunrises in the cupola).
Reduce pending tasks before bed.
Check noise and temperature.
Re-evaluate the next night.

guides.title: Blood glucose (postprandial)
guides.message: Glucose after eating is above normal. Review the meal and measure later.
guides.action: Glucose after eating is above normal. Review the meal and measure later.
steps: Glucose after eating is above normal. Review the meal and measure later.

guides.title: PHQ-9 (depression)
guides.message: Mild mood symptoms (PHQ-9: 6/27). Review your sleep, workload and routine. The test will be repeated in 1–2 weeks.
guides.action: Preventive observation; review sleep hygiene and workload; repeat in 1–2 weeks.
steps: Cross-check items 3 and 4 with real sleep data; if tiredness explains the score, note it before escalating.
Review workload, rest time and social contact with the crew.
Encourage communication with family / psychological support on Earth.
Repeat the PHQ-9 in 1–2 weeks.
If the score stays the same or rises, move to the Orange protocol.

guides.title: GAD-7 (anxiety)
guides.message: Mild anxiety symptoms (GAD-7: 5/21). Review stress sources, sleep and workload.
guides.action: Preventive observation; review stress sources, sleep and workload; repeat in 1–2 weeks.
steps: Review recent stressors (tasks, isolation, crew conflict, communication delay).
Cross-check with sleep and resting heart rate.
Suggest relaxation and breathing exercises, and exercise per the schedule.
If total is 8 or more: flag as a probable case (cutoff of 8 = sensitivity 92 %, specificity 76 %) and recommend a further assessment by the medical officer.
Repeat the GAD-7 in 1–2 weeks.
